newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Guterres optimistic on EMU stability pact.
newsitem.headline: Guterres optimistic on EMU stability pact.

text.p: Portuguese Prime Minister Antonio Guterres said on Wednesday that it should be possible to reach accord on the stability pact, a key element in the European Union's planned single currency, to take account of French demands for a commitment to fight unemployment.
"I think it will be perfectly possible, given willingness on all sides, to conciliate both points of view," Guterres said.

But he declined to be drawn on whether a deal could be done at next week's summit meeting at which the stability pact, committing future single currency members to tight fiscal discipline, is due to be signed.
"We are not worried about one week or two," Guterres told journalists.
"What interests us is that the objectives, which for us are fundamental, are not delayed. These objectives are the single currency in 1999 and a serious European policy for employment," he added.

Guterres said that the Portuguese government would be working actively to reconcile French concerns about unemployment, which he said his Socialist government shared, and Germany's insistence that the stability pact must not be weakened.

France's Socialist-led government said on Monday that the stability pact, with its focus on budgetary discipline, needed to be balanced by an equally tough commitment to boossting employment in Europe.
Guterres did not say how the gap between the two countries, expected to be the two main pillars of the future single currency, would be bridged.
However, he noted that France had not questioned the economic criteria laid down in the Maastricht Treaty for access to the single currency nor the timing of its launch in January 1999.
